I graded s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 items correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | Riley chose "the model opens the booking system itself". The model only writes the tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a loop that repeats itself. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | Riley answered 1 and said the model runs the 3 tools itself. The right answer is 4 model calls: 3 tool requests plus the final answer. |
| q5 | partial | Riley said the result goes back to the model but gave no reason. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Riley was right that the model picks from the tool descriptions. Riley also claimed the model remembers earlier sessions on its own. |

**Summary:** Riley understands the loop and how the model chooses a tool. The open problem is M4: the program runs the tools, not the model. It cost Riley q2 and q4.

The `grade-reviewer` subagent found two problems and I fixed both. The q2 feedback pointed to a lesson that doesn't exist in this workspace. The summary named two things to work on instead of one.

I also wrote `learning-records/0003-program-runs-the-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md` with the open misconceptions. s2 is still ungraded.

**Next step:** Riley should trace the laser cutter request on paper again and write "model" or "program" next to each step.
